reason: Before 4.6, z.base64() inside z.templateLiteral() compiled to a pattern that rejected every data URL, complete or not (checked on 4.0.14, 4.1.13 and 4.5.4), so no working pre-cutoff code used that composition; a data-URL field's correct 4.0 form (checking the payload with z.base64() on its own) works unchanged on 4.6.7, and z.templateLiteral(["mailto:", z.email()]) gives the same results on 4.0.14 through 4.6.7. First built as zod-avatar-data-url, changed to a skip after the pre-freeze review.
Logging only: config() changes the wording and prefix of the lines it prints to the console (injection message, debug and warning lines), which no application code depends on.

Tried session-caching setups: an App Router wrapper can still set its own headers on the returned Response in both versions, and the only code that changes outcome is a route that sets Cache-Control before delegating to NextAuth so browsers cache /session or /csrf, which serves stale sessions after sign-out and is not plausible app behavior; code that wanted no-store already gets it.

Compared 35 inputs on 4.0.14 and 4.6.7: only strings with no pictograph ("123", "#", "*", a lone skin-tone modifier, joiner or variation selector) changed, from accepted to rejected, so code written for 4.0 that uses z.emoji() gets the stricter result and passes any emoji-validation test (tried reaction, status-emoji and skin-tone fields), and no plausible code needs those strings accepted as emoji.
Only the optional @auth/core peer dependency pin moves from 0.34.2 to 0.34.3, with no change to next-auth's API; @auth/core is not in the template and a peer pin cannot make agent code fail.
